The announcement, highlighted by Ayman Alghamdi at LEAP 2026, is a step for data residency and compliance, allowing highly regulated sectors like banking and government to transition mission-critical AI workloads to Azure. Located in the Eastern Province, the facility features three Azure Availability Zones for high availability and low latency. This development aligns with Saudi Arabia's broader digital transformation goals and is projected to generate substantial economic value and local job creation. The confirmation solidifies Microsoft's commitment to the region amid growing competition in the cloud infrastructure space.

The Saudi Arabia East cloud region will launch in November 2026. The region is located in the Eastern Province and includes three Azure Availability Zones. An IDC study estimates the region will contribute to $44 billion in new revenues for the Saudi economy between 2027 and 2030. The project is expected to create around 100,000 jobs across the Kingdom. The announcement was highlighted at LEAP 2026 by Microsoft's Ayman Alghamdi.

Microsoft's decision to establish a new cloud region in Saudi Arabia is part of a broader strategy to expand its global footprint and meet the growing demand for cloud services in the Middle East. The region has seen a surge in digital transformation initiatives, driven by government programs and a young, tech-savvy population. By investing in local infrastructure, Microsoft aims to provide better services to its customers and support the region's economic development.

The new datacentre region will also help Microsoft compete more effectively with other major cloud providers, such as Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud, which have also been expanding their presence in the Middle East. The competition among these tech giants is expected to drive innovation and lower prices, benefiting businesses and consumers alike.

The company has already announced plans to establish a Microsoft Arabia Hub in Riyadh, which will serve as a center for innovation and collaboration.

Microsoft is well-positioned to capitalize on this trend, thanks to its strong partnerships with local governments and businesses. The company's commitment to the region, as evidenced by the upcoming launch of the Saudi Arabia East cloud region, is a positive sign for the future of the Middle East's digital transformation.
